reason: Prior evidence shows the active panel32 path already reuses each loaded A and B vector across two FMOPA operations and updates all four ZA tiles. I rank schedules that retain this reuse without adding live vectors first: interleaving pointer updates may use existing FMOPA work to cover their cost, while the two-step pipeline could hide load latency but raises register-pressure risk. Counter and prefetch changes are smaller tests, though prior counter results were mixed and distance-4 prefetch regressed on the inactive path. Layout, fusion, padding, and microbuffer proposals add packing or loop work without measured support; direct A transpose affects the fallback, not the n=512 timed path. These are experiment priorities, not predictions of measured gains or causes.
